title: Punch-Drunk Love
full_review:
"Punch-Drunk Love" (Columbia) brings together angry loner Adam Sandler and would-be girlfriend Emily Watson in one of the least-engaging romances in years.

Writer-director Thomas Paul Anderson created the role of misfit Barry Egan specifically for Sandler, and perhaps his fans will find humor and pathos in his character. However, many others are more likely to find Sandler and the entire film not, as intended, goofy-charming, but downright annoying.

Alienated and rage-filled, Barry operates a Los Angelesnovelties warehouse but is often distracted by phone calls from his seven overbearing sisters. When frustrated, he is prone to smashing furniture, or kicking out glass patio doors when his siblings tease him. Nonetheless, Lena(Watson), a friend of one sister, after seeing his photo, asks him to dinner and urges him to join her in Hawaiion a business trip. What she doesn't know is that hapless Barry has been targeted by a group of phone-sex scam artists in Utahwho mistakenly think he's a wealthy entrepreneur and four of them head for LA to rob him blind.

A somewhat amusing subplot involves Barry visiting supermarkets to buy $3,000 worth of instant pudding cups in order to get a lifetime's worth of frequent-flyer miles -- based on an actual incident -- but more often Barry's mindless staring into space is just tiresome. Philip Seymour Hoffman plays one of the phone-sex creeps whose profane mouth is forever screaming curses, which Sandler returns in kind. How desperately unfunny that is. In what is supposed to be a romantic comedy, the humor is as flat as the music track is obtrusive. And the sudden spurts of violence between the four thugs and Barry isentirely out of keeping with what should have been a light, entertainingly quirky comedy.

Due to brief violence, crude sexual references, an implied sexual encounter, minimal profanity and much rough language, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R--restricted.
